display.purpose: The role line of the cover title, once per page.

display-name.purpose: The name line 12px above the display line, completing the title lockup.

numeral.purpose: Step numbers: Construction Grey at rest, Part Orange, Right Face on the current step.

headline.purpose: Section headings, the helpline question included.

headline-contact.purpose: The email address on the helpline, underlined 3px.

title.purpose: Step titles in the assembly sequence.

title-part.purpose: Part names in the parts tray.

lead.purpose: The promise under the cover title, max 30ch.

body.purpose: Reading text in ink or Soft Ink, 30ch to 70ch.

label.purpose: Navigation links; the same 15px step carries the legend at 500 and captions and table text at 400.

small.purpose: Facts in the ink strip; the colophon at 400 in Soft Ink.

table-head.purpose: Spec-table column and group heads, sentence case.

tag.purpose: The letter inside a circled part tag.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out shared by every slide, nudge and colour change. It never overshoots.

motion.name: part-slide
motion.purpose: A part travels along its explosion line into its seat.

motion.name: mark-snap
motion.purpose: Click marks, the detail circle and the done tick switch on in a single frame once the slide has landed.

motion.name: colour-change
motion.purpose: A part's faces turn to the orange set while it is the newest part; the current step numeral changes colour on the same timing.

motion.name: explode-switch
motion.purpose: An explosion line switches off the moment its part starts to slide in, and back on when the part leaves.

motion.name: control-hover
motion.purpose: Orange controls shift to Part Orange, Left Face on hover.

motion.name: arrow-nudge
motion.purpose: The primary button's arrow slides 4px toward the action on hover.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The primary button drops 1px while pressed, with no transition.

motion.name: anchor-scroll
motion.purpose: In-page jumps glide and clear the sticky masthead.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every state appears at once, without movement.

narrative.overview:
The site is printed like the manual in a flat-pack box: uncoated paper, one black ink and a single process orange. Anything that explains is drawn as 30° isometric line art, with circled part letters, dashed explosion lines, a detail circle and click marks. Anything that reads is set in one Norwegian grotesk, blunt at 900 and plain at 400. Orange appears only where something is happening: on the part going in, and at the place to act.

The system is flat and literal. There are no cards, boxes, shadows or visible gradients. Only the manual's own devices frame content: 2px ink rules, circled letters on leader lines, the detail circle and the ink fact strip. Depth exists only inside the drawings, where every solid has three face tones. Explanation gets air and proof gets packed: drawings sit alone on the dot lattice, while facts run in a dense ink strip and the work is listed in a ruled spec table. Motion is mechanical. A part slides along its explosion line on an exponential ease-out and lands with a click mark that switches on in a single frame.

The page stays on paper in every OS theme; the dark theme was removed in review and is not part of the world. The system refuses the developer-portfolio defaults (a dark hero, skill-icon grids, equal project cards) and, as a brand commitment, AI-hype imagery: glowing gradients, robots, neural-network visuals.
keyCharacteristics: Manual Paper and one Manual Ink; the page never goes dark.
Part Orange only on the part being added and the place to act.
30° isometric line drawings with three face tones, circled part letters, dashed explosion lines, a detail circle and click marks.
One family, Schibsted Grotesk 400–900, ranked by weight, with heavy tabular numerals.
Flat: no cards, boxes, shadows or visible gradients.
Mechanical motion: slide along the explosion line, then click.

rules.name: The Two Places Rule
rules.body: Part Orange marks exactly two things: the part being added, and the place to act. Links, headings, icons, rules and decoration are never orange; text selection borrows it as a highlight.

rules.name: The Current Part Rule
rules.body: In a step sequence, the current step's numeral turns from Construction Grey to Part Orange, Right Face: the shaded tone of the part going into the drawing, at 4.5:1 on paper. Part Orange itself never sets text on paper.

rules.name: The Paper Edition Rule
rules.body: There is one edition, printed on paper. No dark theme and no dark-mode variant; the fact strip is the only band printed on an ink ground.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: One family, ranked by weight: 900 for display, numerals and the wordmark; 800 for headings and titles; 700 for actions, tags and table heads; 600 for navigation; 400 and 500 for reading. No second face, no uppercase, no tracked-out labels.

rules.name: The Heavy Numeral Rule
rules.body: Sequence numbers are huge, black-weight, tightly tracked and tabular. They show state by colour alone, never by size.

rules.name: The Five-and-Seven Rule
rules.body: Where words and a drawing share a row, the words take five columns and the drawing takes seven.

rules.name: The Drawing Board Rule
rules.body: The lattice belongs to drawings. It appears only behind surfaces that carry them, and it never sets out the blocks.

rules.name: The Three-Face Rule
rules.body: Every solid is drawn in three tones with light from the upper left: the top face is Manual Paper, the left face Left Face, the right face Right Face. The part being added swaps all three for Part Orange and its two shade faces; nothing else about it changes.

rules.name: The No-Cast-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow: not the controls, not the photograph, not the drawings. Depth comes from face tone and ink outline only.

rules.name: The Manual Devices Rule
rules.body: Only the manual's own devices frame content: ink rules, circled letters on leader lines, the detail circle and the ink fact strip. No cards, boxes, outlined panels or pills.

rules.name: The Slide-and-Click Rule
rules.body: Parts move one way only: along their own explosion line, into their seat, on the exponential ease-out. Marks of state switch on in a single frame once the slide lands, and nothing fades in from invisible.

dos: Do keep the page on Manual Paper (#f4f4f1) and print everything that states something in Manual Ink (#141414).
Do keep Part Orange (#ff5a1f) for the part being added and the place to act, with ink text and ink focus rings on it.

Do draw every illustration as 30° isometric line art: ink outlines (1.6 drawing units in assemblies, 2 for single parts), three face tones lit from the upper left, round joins, and circled letters on leader lines.
Do frame content only with the manual's devices: 2px ink rules, circled part letters, the detail circle and the ink fact strip.
Do rank type by Schibsted Grotesk's weights (900 display and numerals, 800 headings, 700 actions, 400 reading) and stay in the one family.
Do move parts by sliding them along their dashed explosion lines on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), and switch marks of state on in a single frame once the slide lands.
Do show every state without movement under reduced motion, and show the finished assembly when JavaScript is off.
Do print photographs in ink on orange (grayscale, 1.1 contrast, multiply), and let only the film play in full colour.
donts: Don't add cards, boxes, outlined panels, drop shadows or visible gradients such as glows and colour ramps. The lattice's hard-stop dots are a pattern, not a gradient.
Don't ship a dark theme or a dark-mode variant; the page stays on paper in every OS theme.
Don't use Part Orange for decoration, links, headings or icons, or for any text on paper (2.8:1); text that marks the current part takes Part Orange, Right Face.
Don't set Construction Grey (#8c8c86) text below display size; it measures 3.1:1 on paper.
Don't use AI-hype imagery: glowing gradients, robots, neural-network visuals.
Don't put kickers or eyebrow labels over headings, set labels in uppercase or tracked caps, or add a second typeface.
Don't fade elements in from invisible or let them overshoot; state changes slide or switch.
Don't use glyph characters or icon fonts as icons; the manual's marks (arrow, click, tick) are drawn strokes in inline SVG.
Don't round corners past 6px or use pills; circles are kept for the manual's marks.
